citation.authors: Valbuena VSM, Seelye S, Sjoding MW, Valley TS et al

record.population: 30,039 paired readings in general-care inpatients, Veterans Health Administration, 2013-2019 (21.6% from non-Hispanic Black patients)
record.design: Multicentre retrospective cohort comparing pulse oximetry (SpO2) with arterial blood gas (SaO2) within 10 minutes
record.finding: Among SpO2 readings of 92% or more, the unadjusted probability of occult hypoxaemia (SaO2 below 88%) was 15.6% in white patients and 19.6% in black patients (P<0.001, similar in adjusted models). The authors say this could limit access to oxygen and other treatment for black patients.
record.note: US veterans, mostly white; race from records; skin tone itself was not measured.
